Meta Test Description: This testcase validates MIPI CSI-2 DPHY lane configuration by iterating through lane counts from 4 down to 1. It first enables CSI-2 interrupts by reading MIZAR_MIPI_CSI2_HOST_INT_ST_MAIN to clear pending interrupts, then writing all interrupt mask registers (INT_MSK_PHY_FATAL, INT_MSK_PKT_FATAL, INT_MSK_PHY, INT_MSK_LINE, INT_MSK_BNDRY_FRAME_FATAL, INT_MSK_SEQ_FRAME_FATAL, INT_MSK_CRC_FRAME_FATAL, INT_MSK_PLD_CRC_FATAL, INT_MSK_DATA_ID, INT_MSK_ECC_CORRECTED). It configures the virtual channel register MIZAR_MIPI_CSI2_RB_REG_VIRTUAL_CHANNEL based on the selected GDMA path (GDMA0/1/2/3) and enables control data transfer via MIZAR_MIPI_CSI2_RB_REG_CONTROL_DATA. After D-PHY initialization via snps_phy_init(), it polls MIZAR_MIPI_CSI2_HOST_PHY_STOPSTATE until the value equals 0x1000f (indicating all lanes in stop state). For each lane configuration (3 down to 0), it writes MIZAR_MIPI_CSI2_HOST_N_LANES with the lane count, triggers the CSI-2 sequence by writing to 0xa0243ffc, then loops through control and data packets using DMA transfers. Each iteration programs DMA instructions, starts DMA via DMAGO_CSI, polls DMA interrupt status (MIPI_CSI2_DMA_INTMIS_OFFSET) for completion, clears DMA interrupts (MIPI_CSI2_DMA_INTCLR_OFFSET), reads control data from 0xE6001000, extracts word_count and data_type, and if data_type > 0xf, programs a second DMA channel for CSI data transfer with calculated csi_data_size aligned to 8 bytes. The test completes by calling finish(0).
Test Description: This test validates MIPI CSI-2 DPHY lane configuration by iterating through all supported lane counts (4 lanes down to 1 lane). It enables all CSI-2 interrupt masks, configures the virtual channel based on the selected GDMA path, enables control data transfer, initializes the D-PHY, and polls the PHY stop state register until all lanes reach stop state. For each lane configuration, it programs the number of active lanes, triggers the CSI-2 sequence, and performs DMA-based transfers for both control packets and data packets. Each packet transfer involves programming DMA instructions, starting DMA, polling for DMA interrupt completion, clearing the interrupt, and reading back control data to determine if a data payload transfer is needed. Data payload size is calculated from the word count field and aligned to 8 bytes before initiating the data DMA transfer.

Meta Test Description: This testcase validates the default reset values and write/read accessibility of all MIPI CSI-2 RB REG block registers. It defines 10 register addresses in addr_array[] (MIZAR_MIPI_CSI2_RB_REG_VIRTUAL_CHANNEL, MIZAR_MIPI_CSI2_RB_REG_LINE_INFO, MIZAR_MIPI_CSI2_RB_REG_FIFO_THRESHOLD_VAL, MIZAR_MIPI_CSI2_RB_REG_LANE_CLK, MIZAR_MIPI_CSI2_RB_REG_MEM, MIZAR_MIPI_CSI2_RB_REG_INTERRUPT_RAW, MIZAR_MIPI_CSI2_RB_REG_INTERRUPT_MASK, MIZAR_MIPI_CSI2_RB_REG_INTERRUPT_ENABLE, MIZAR_MIPI_CSI2_RB_REG_CONTROL_DATA, MIZAR_MIPI_CSI2_RB_REG_FLUSH) along with corresponding default_value_array[], read_mask_array[], write_mask_array[], and skip_array[]. The test first calls chk_rst_val() which iterates through all registers, skipping those with read_mask_array[i]==0x00000000, reads each register via read_reg(addr), and compares the read value against default_value_array[i], incrementing def_fail_cnt on mismatch. Then chk_rd_wr() iterates through 6 test patterns (chk_val[6]={0xffffffff, 0xaaaaaaaa, 0x55555555, 0x00000000, 0xA5A5A5A5, 0xffff0000}). For each pattern, it writes to all writable registers (skipping those in skip_array or with write_mask_array==0x00000000) via write_reg(addr, data_wr), then reads back each register via read_reg(addr). The expected value is computed as exp_val = ((data_wr & read_mask_array[i] & write_mask_array[i]) | (wr_n & read_mask_array[i] & default_value_array[i])) where wr_n = (write_mask_array[i] ^ 0xffffffff). If data_rd != exp_val, wr_fail_cnt is incremented. The soft_reset_chk() function is commented out in test_case(). The test calls finish(0) if both def_fail_cnt and wr_fail_cnt are 0, otherwise finish(1). Registers at skip_array indices 5 (MIZAR_MIPI_CSI2_RB_REG_INTERRUPT_RAW) and 9 (MIZAR_MIPI_CSI2_RB_REG_FLUSH) are skipped during write/read checks.
Test Description: This test validates the default reset values and write/read accessibility of all registers in the MIPI CSI-2 RB REG block. It first reads each register and compares the value against its expected default reset value. Then it writes six different test patterns to all writable registers and reads them back, computing the expected value using the register's read mask, write mask, and default value to account for read-only bits. Registers flagged in a skip array (interrupt_raw and flush) are excluded from write/read verification. The test passes only if all default value checks and all write/read-back comparisons succeed across all six test patterns for all applicable registers.

For each register, check if read_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000; if so, skip (register not readable). 3. Call read_reg(addr_array[i]) and store result in data_rd. 4. Compare data_rd against default_value_array[i]; if mismatch, increment def_fail_cnt and print failure. 5. Call chk_rd_wr(): define chk_val[6] = {0xffffffff, 0xaaaaaaaa, 0x55555555, 0x00000000, 0xA5A5A5A5, 0xffff0000}. 6. Loop j from 0 to 5 over chk_val[]. 7. Set data_wr = chk_val[j]. 8. Write phase: iterate i from 0 to CNT-1 over addr_array[]. 9. For each register, check skip_array[i] == 1; if so, skip. 10. Check write_mask_array[i] == 0x00000000; if so, skip (register not writable). 11. Call write_reg(addr_array[i], data_wr). 12. Read phase: iterate i from 0 to CNT-1 over addr_array[]. 13-19. Read back, compute expected, compare. 20. After all patterns and registers, check if def_fail_cnt > 0 or wr_fail_cnt > 0; if so, call finish(1), else call finish(0).
Test Steps / Procedure: 1. Read each register in the RB REG block and verify that the value matches its expected default reset value, skipping registers that are not readable. 2. For each of six test patterns (all-ones, alternating 0xAA, alternating 0x55, all-zeros, 0xA5A5A5A5, 0xFFFF0000): a. Write the test pattern to all writable registers, skipping registers flagged in the skip array or marked as not writable. b. Read back each written register, skipping non-readable or non-writable registers. c. Compute the expected read-back value by applying the register's read mask, write mask, and default value to account for read-only bit positions. d. Compare the actual read value against the computed expected value. 3. Verify that all default value checks passed with zero failures. 4. Verify that all write/read-back checks passed with zero failures across all six test patterns. 5. Confirm the test reports a pass result only if no mismatches were detected.

Feature: DPHY IDI Virtual Channel Data Transfer with Null and Blanking
Meta Test Description: This testcase validates MIPI CSI-2 DPHY IDI data transfer across all 16 virtual channels (vcid 0 to 15) with null and blanking data enabled. It first calls snps_phy_init() for D-PHY initialization, then calls csi2_enable_interrupt() which reads MIZAR_MIPI_CSI2_HOST_INT_ST_MAIN to clear pending interrupts and writes all interrupt mask registers. It polls MIZAR_MIPI_CSI2_HOST_PHY_STOPSTATE until 0x1000f. It enables control data and null/blanking transfer. For each vcid (0-15), it configures virtual channel, triggers transfer, and processes 129 packets via DMA with conditional data payload transfers.
Test Description: This test validates MIPI CSI-2 DPHY IDI data transfer across all 16 virtual channels (0 through 15) with both null and blanking data transfer enabled. It initializes the D-PHY, enables all CSI-2 interrupt masks, and polls the PHY stop state register until all lanes reach stop state. Control data transfer and null/blanking data transfer are both enabled. For each of the 16 virtual channels, the virtual channel register is configured, a trigger is sent to start packet transfer on the selected channel, and 129 control packets are processed via DMA. Each control packet transfer involves programming and starting DMA on channel 0, polling for DMA completion, clearing the interrupt, and reading back the control data. If the control data indicates an image data packet (data type greater than 0xf), a second DMA transfer is initiated on channel 1 for the data payload with size calculated from the word count field and aligned to 8 bytes. The test passes after all 16 virtual channels complete their full packet sequences.

Remarks: This test iterates through all 16 virtual channels (vcid 0 to 15), unlike other MIPI CSI-2 tests that use a single compile-time selected GDMA path. The virtual channel register is configured with vcid shifted to bits [15:12] only (vcid<<12), using only GDMA0 path. Both control data and null/blanking data transfers are enabled simultaneously. Each virtual channel processes 129 control packets. Two hardcoded register addresses are used that could not be mapped to named registers in the specification. The data payload size is aligned to 8-byte boundaries. The D-PHY initialization is performed via an external function snps_phy_init().
